turns.text: That's an intriguing concept! While there's no scientific consensus on the idea that bad ideas increase during daylight, it might be related to the way our minds work—sometimes we need to confront problems head-on (daylight) before we can see solutions more clearly. Conversely, the quiet of night could foster a different kind of thinking. Creativity often thrives in unexpected places; it’s about how we frame and approach our ideas.
